Warned Hjumpik about Toad Lee.
Tossed Hjumpik the key and left to gain time.
morel_feyward_key.waluigi: A key from Morel is never only a key. It is an invitation to owe uncertainty rent.
morel_feyward_key.description: A key tossed to Hjumpik by Mystic Morel after warning him not to make Toad Lee the anchor. A key from Morel is never only a key. It is an invitation to owe uncertainty rent.

oc_soul_ring.name: The OC Soul Ring
oc_soul_ring.summary: A heavy gold ring designed to capture souls, engraved inside the band with the initials OC. Recovered from the false Lady Aurelian — the Feyward manor’s overgrowth wearing its owner’s face — who cheerfully admitted she struck the real Aurelian in the stomach mid-flight and trapped her in the ring. Currently in Hjumpik’s custody, in the same pocket as Morel’s key, which says something unkind about Hjumpik’s pocket.
oc_soul_ring.obtained: Blown off the plant lady’s finger by an indoor Bob-omb, grabbed mid-skid by Waluigi, and deposited with the Anvil for absolutely non-negotiable custody.
features: Captures souls. One reported occupant: the actual Lady of the manor.
Band engraved ‘OC’ — the same initials carved into Corvinarus bedframes.
Chain of custody this evening: her → Waluigi → her → Waluigi → Hjumpik.
Warm as a wrist, which Waluigi finds rude.
history: Catalogued jewelry-side at the false Lady’s own table (Waluigi catalogues all jewelry).
Looted by Waluigi during the second hidden room rout; reclaimed by its owner via direct air-freight; reclaimed again by Waluigi via indoor explosives.
Explained by a defected guard who had been planning to take it to ‘the actual lady’ himself.
Final custody, pending everything: Hjumpik Deldkur, of Karaz Ankor, who does not hjump on this particular decision quickly.
oc_soul_ring.waluigi: Do not smash it, do not sell it, do not let Wario appraise it, and under no circumstances — including formal occasions — does anyone WEAR the soul jar.
oc_soul_ring.description: Waluigi is filing the OC Soul Ring as soul hardware, not jewelry, because the difference matters the way the difference between a door and a wall matters. It captures souls; it has one in it already, by the cheerful testimony of the manor’s overgrowth; and its band carries the same two initials that turn up carved into the bedframes of the Corvinarus Sanctum — OC, the mark the archive has tied to the Oracle, whoever the Oracle is this week. Its practical value resists pricing, which did not stop Wario from asking. What matters is custody. The ring changed hands four times in one night and every transfer cost the room a piece of its dignity; it now rests in the pocket of the only dwarf in the branch who treats other people’s souls with the correct paperwork. Handling guidance: interview the occupant through a professional; find the plant’s private sanctuary before she finishes unpacking; and keep the ring away from any limb with a price stamp on it. If the party ignores this guidance, Waluigi will not be surprised, but Waluigi will be annoyed in advance. WAH.

waluigi_disguise_kit_wally.name: Waluigi’s Disguise Kit (‘Wally’)
waluigi_disguise_kit_wally.summary: A leather pouch containing the remnants of Waluigi’s greatest acting role: a forged Iron Legion identification card for ‘Wally,’ a mustache-less scout from the 4th Recon Division, plus the small razor used to shave his iconic mustache for the role, spirit gum, and a collection of fake noses. Kept in pristine condition as proof of superior intellect and espionage capability, despite the disastrous end to the mission aboard the Vigilance.
waluigi_disguise_kit_wally.obtained: Commissioned for the Vigilance infiltration; carried ever since, through every theater, out of pride, preparedness, and spite.
features: Forged Iron Legion ID: ‘Wally,’ 4th Recon Division. Mustache: conspicuously absent.
Razor, spirit gum, and a row of noses for face-level contingencies.
Deployed in the Feyward war room with the offer ‘a fake mustache, or a nose.’
Documented fool-count: zero. Dignity: intact.
history: Shaved the mustache for the role, which is the most Waluigi thing to have ever happened for operational reasons.
Survived the mission’s disastrous end aboard the Vigilance; the kit, unlike the mission, was preserved in pristine condition, because the kit was the good part.
Offered publicly in the heir’s war room: ‘I can put on a fake mustache. Or a nose.’ Answered by Hjumpik: ‘You’re in the same outfit. You’re not fooling anyone.’
waluigi_disguise_kit_wally.waluigi: The mustache grew back. The legend never had to. WAH.
waluigi_disguise_kit_wally.description: Waluigi is filing the disguise kit as proof of concept, and the concept is that Waluigi is an actor of considerable range betrayed by his surroundings. The kit itself is flawless: a forged identification card that would pass a checkpoint, spirit gum of professional tack, noses arranged in ascending order of believability. Its failure record is not the kit’s fault. Waluigi in another outfit is Wally, scout of the 4th Recon Division, master of the crate-lid school of surveillance. Waluigi in the SAME outfit is Waluigi with a nose on, which fools nobody, which Hjumpik stated aloud in a war room, in front of noses. The pouch remains in pristine condition. Given the right war, the right checkpoint, and the right hat, the kit will rise again. One of the kit's [[prop:prop_ebot_passport|forged travel documents]] survives in the archive — issued at Mount Ebot, photographed as nobody in particular, never once presented to a checkpoint. Handling guidance: do not laugh at the kit. The kit has done things. If the party ignores this guidance, Waluigi will not be surprised, but Waluigi will make a note of it on a fake mustache application form.

raventree_signet_ring.name: The Raventree Signet Ring
raventree_signet_ring.summary: A signet ring found in the grass on a table in Lady Aurelian’s dark bedroom and recognised by Hjumpik on sight. It can create and destroy connections between the fractured manors: it can speed the ritual of opening the portal, or sever the link entirely. In Hjumpik’s pocket since ~19 Harvestide, 1040 BF (Feyward time).
raventree_signet_ring.obtained: Hjumpik bumped into a table in the dark, squished something that smelled strong, reached into the grass and found the ring under it.
features: Creates or destroys connections between the manors — a key that can lock and unlock doors, install new ones and take old ones off their frames.
Can accelerate the portal-opening ritual, or sever the connection outright.
The Book of Revised History, found the same hour, warns the manors must not be combined while a star shard is in play; the ring can honour that warning or ignore it.
Not the OC Soul Ring — that one came off the false Lady’s finger four nights later and is a different object.
history: Found on a table in Lady Aurelian’s overgrown bedroom, ~19 Harvestide, 1040 BF.
Recognised by Hjumpik immediately; Waluigi records that his reading of its functions was correct.
Carried in Hjumpik’s pocket since, shown to nobody — including the Colour Division, who were bought ten minutes with it unseen.
raventree_signet_ring.waluigi: The ring does not have an opinion about which function is correct. The question is not what the ring can do. The question is who gets to decide what the ring does.
raventree_signet_ring.description: Waluigi is filing the Raventree Signet Ring as a manor key and not as jewellery, because a key that can also remove the door belongs in the custody column and not the treasure column. It was found where chaos left it, or where Aurelian arranged for it to be found, or where the house put it; Waluigi holds all three theories and likes none of them. Its two functions — merge and sever — are the two ends of the Feyward crisis, and the decision about which one to use is now the single most important decision in the party’s hands. The hands are Hjumpik’s. He has not hjumped to it.

book_of_revised_history.name: The Book of Revised History
book_of_revised_history.summary: A book Hjumpik picked out of the vegetation by the couch in Aurelian’s rooms and pocketed like a receipt from a shop. It records Raventree Manor in the 980s BF as a thriving academic centre where Toads, orcs and lightning professors exchanged ideas freely, a proto-Liberated Toads movement there ‘enlightened’ by the Iron Legion and then the Mages Guild, and a warning that the manors must not be combined while a star shard is in play.
book_of_revised_history.obtained: Resting on or near the couch, partly buried in leaves, not destroyed; Hjumpik identified it, examined it, handed it to Waluigi to read, and put it in his pocket.
features: Raventree in the 980s BF was a school, not a horror: Toads, orcs and lightning professors in free exchange.
A proto-Liberated Toads movement at Raventree was ‘enlightened’ — suppressed — by the Iron Legion and then the Mages Guild, sixty years before Order 120.
The manors must NOT be combined while a star shard is in play; the Oracle’s plan requires exactly that.
Hjumpik’s level of engagement on reading it: background lore. Waluigi’s: among the most important intelligence of the Feyward campaign.
history: Found in the vegetation of Lady Aurelian’s rooms, ~19 Harvestide, 1040 BF.
Read in full by Waluigi, who reproduced the passages in the session record.
Carried by Hjumpik since.
book_of_revised_history.waluigi: My colleagues have a persistent, infuriating habit of finding historically critical documents and treating them like grocery lists.
book_of_revised_history.description: Waluigi is filing the Book of Revised History as historical intelligence because it is the only document in the archive that puts the Legion–Guild axis sixty years before the current crisis, at the same manor, crushing the same kind of movement. The vocabulary changes. The boot does not. The book also carries the one warning that bears directly on the Raventree Signet Ring found minutes later: do not combine the manors. The two objects live in the same pocket, which is either poetry or a filing error.

woodfellow_library_card.name: Woodfellow Library Card
woodfellow_library_card.summary: A card to Woodfellow’s library in the Feyward manor, given to Hjumpik by the goblin patron Artameer Fellow during the Revel crisis (~18 Harvestide, 1040 BF). Woodfellow issues cards only to people he assesses as genuinely knowledgeable; the return policy is one week, or the borrower becomes a book.
woodfellow_library_card.obtained: Given to Hjumpik in the library after he found ‘Concerning the Nature and Sustenance of Revels Eternal’; Artameer Fellow is the patron whose previous card Wario stole to check out the Feyward Book of Many Things.
features: Access to Woodfellow’s library and its rare fey texts.
One week to return a book, or the borrower becomes a book. Woodfellow is equanimous about this.
Issued on an assessment of knowledge — a credential with actual standards, which Waluigi notes was not extended to Waluigi.
history: Artameer’s earlier card was stolen by Wario and used to check out, sell and gut the Feyward Book of Many Things.
Hjumpik received his own card from Artameer Fellow in the Revel crisis session.
Carried by Hjumpik since; not yet used to borrow anything on the record.
woodfellow_library_card.waluigi: The transformation-as-late-fee system is the most effective library enforcement mechanism Waluigi has encountered in any documented plane.
woodfellow_library_card.description: Waluigi is filing the library card as a credential rather than a trinket because in the Feyward a credential is a contract with a tree, and this particular tree turns late borrowers into shelving. The card is the party’s legitimate route back into the Woodfellow stacks, which matters now that the Book of Revised History has told us what the stacks might know. It was issued to Hjumpik on the strength of his knowledge. Waluigi has made his position on that assessment clear elsewhere and will not repeat it here more than once.

colour_division_handcuffs.name: Colour Division Handcuffs
colour_division_handcuffs.summary: A pair of Iron Legion handcuffs put on Waluigi by the Colour Division on the upper landing of the Overgrown Manor when he and Toad Lee were taken as leverage against Hjumpik’s overdue Aegis Magi contract (2 Aethel, 922 BF, Feyward clock). Waluigi slipped them immediately and stood there wearing them anyway, because there is no theatre in an empty cuff.
colour_division_handcuffs.obtained: Produced by Red after Hjumpik put a hand on his warhammer and said ‘No cages. They’re not animals. Just hold them.’ The Division agreed without argument.
features: Cuffs rather than mage cages — Hjumpik’s condition, accepted without argument, which worried Waluigi more than a refusal would have.
Slipped at once; worn by choice for the theatre of it.
Still on Waluigi’s wrists, open, at the end of the session; the Division has not noticed.
history: Put on Waluigi and Toad Lee on the upper landing as leverage.
Out of them before anybody noticed; not mentioned to the Division.
Kept on, as a prop, through the stair-door standoff.
colour_division_handcuffs.waluigi: I slipped the handcuffs immediately and stood there wearing them anyway, because there is no theatre in an empty cuff.
colour_division_handcuffs.description: Waluigi is filing the handcuffs because the archive files custody, and for one evening the custody was Waluigi’s. They are Legion issue, competent, and open. They stay on the record as the only piece of Colour Division property the party currently holds, and on Waluigi’s wrists as the only piece of Colour Division property the Division currently believes it holds. Both facts are useful. Neither has been mentioned to Red.

hjumpik_wolf_pelt_onesie.name: Hjumpik’s Wolf-Pelt Onesie
hjumpik_wolf_pelt_onesie.summary: The wolf-pelt onesie Hjumpik has worn for three Feyward sessions. The Colour Division identified him by it from a doorway — not by description, sigil or writ — and his defence that all dwarves use wolf pelt did not land.
hjumpik_wolf_pelt_onesie.obtained: Worn. The record does not say where it came from; it says who recognised it.
features: Signature garment: ‘Hey — you ARE Hjumpik. You have the signature wolf-pelt onesie on.’
Warm, which matters in a manor that keeps rearranging its weather.
Evidence, as of 2 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock). Waluigi had never once thought of it as evidence.
history: Worn through the Feyward sessions since at least the dark rooms.
Used by the Colour Division to identify Hjumpik through a half-open door.
Still on him.
hjumpik_wolf_pelt_onesie.waluigi: Four special forces operatives crossed a planar boundary into a house full of carnivorous architecture to collect one contractor, and the identification was made on a garment.
hjumpik_wolf_pelt_onesie.description: Waluigi is filing the onesie as a garment and as a liability, in that order. It is not armour — Hjumpik’s chain mail is a separate line — and it is not disguise, since its entire documented effect is the opposite. It is what he wears, and what the Legion now looks for. The archive recommends nothing. The archive notes that it has never seen the dwarf without it.

gold.name: Gold Piece
gold.description: Universal trade gold. Banks accept it because weight, purity, and greed are internationally understood languages. Gold is slow to move in bulk but excellent for reserves, vault collateral, and settlements between factions that hate each other but still understand math. Backing: assayed gold weight. Bank note: universal bank reserve.

silver.name: Silver Piece
silver.description: Everyday trade silver. It is common enough for wages and road expenses but stable enough for bank counters to bother counting. Rural banks often prefer silver to exotic scrip because farmers trust a coin they can bite. Backing: assayed silver weight. Bank note: universal small tender.

copper.name: Copper Bit
copper.description: Low-value street currency for bread, candles, cart fees, ferry tips, and market change. Banks accept copper reluctantly in sacks, then charge handling fees because bankers believe suffering should be itemized. Backing: copper weight. Bank note: legal small tender.

midland_ducat.name: Midland Ducat
midland_ducat.description: The Regal Empire’s main bank coin: stable, standardized, taxable, and boring in the way successful money often is. Imperial banks like it because every coin has a known weight, issue date, and paperwork trail. Backing: imperial tax authority and gold reserves. Bank note: legal tender in imperial courts.

imperial_crown.name: Imperial Crown
imperial_crown.description: A heavy state coin backed by census, army, tax office, and a treasury that thinks confidence is a military doctrine. Midlands banks accept Crowns as strong foreign exchange when the paperwork is clean. Backing: state reserves and military payroll. Bank note: recognized foreign exchange.

archive_writ.name: Archive Writ
archive_writ.description: A Regal court writ redeemable for archive fees, sealed copies, transcript searches, and restricted legal documents. Banks treat it like a service draft rather than coin, but it is accepted because courts enforce it. Backing: court service obligations. Bank note: bankable government draft.

mushroom_coin.name: Mushroom Coin
mushroom_coin.description: The old Mushroom Regency coin still circulates in markets, inns, warehouses, and tax offices. Its problem is not metal; its problem is trust. Banks accept it, but many now check which political faction stamped the last transfer. Backing: royal treasury remnants. Bank note: politically strained legal tender.

peach_crown.name: Peach Crown
peach_crown.description: A restoration coin issued by Peach Loyalists to pay soldiers, scouts, surgeons, and supply caravans. Loyalist banks honor it at full confidence; Regency banks accept it only when nobody official is watching. Backing: captured stores and restoration claims. Bank note: rebel tender; bankable in Loyalist areas.

toad_bond.name: Toad Bond
toad_bond.description: A serious rebuilding bond issued by Liberated Toad councils after the Vigilance barrel-trafficking crisis. It funds food, medicine, shelter, tools, prosthetics, and legal defense. Banks that refuse it are usually making a political statement. Backing: donations, recovered cargo, and community repayment. Bank note: bankable community bond in friendly markets.

relief_stamp.name: Relief Stamp
relief_stamp.description: A ration and shelter voucher used by displaced Toad communities. Banks do not love vouchers, but relief banks and Loyalist quartermasters honor them because people need soup before monetary theory. Backing: ration stores and aid ledgers. Bank note: redeemable relief voucher.

decree_strip.name: Decree Strip
decree_strip.description: A narrow legal note used to pay messengers, advocates, witnesses, and safehouse clerks connected to Speaker L’s resistance network. Bankers treat it as risky but real because witness networks can be stronger than kings. Backing: service promises and witness networks. Bank note: restricted resistance note.

beanbean_bean.name: Beanbean Bean
beanbean_bean.description: A bean-shaped regional coin accepted along Mushroom trade roads. It is cheerful, annoying to stack, and surprisingly reliable. Banks like the consistency even when they dislike the joke molded into the edge. Backing: regional taxes and crop trade. Bank note: recognized regional tender.

wario_coin.name: Wario Coin
wario_coin.description: A private gold-weight coin stamped with Wario’s face. Wario Land banks honor it aggressively; other banks accept it after verifying weight and after sighing at the portrait. Wario insists the portrait increases value. Backing: private hoard reserves. Bank note: bankable private tender.

wario_points.name: Wario Points
wario_points.description: Quest-board points spendable at Wario’s shop economy. These are not XP and not normal coin; banks only honor them if they have a direct Wario settlement account. Wario likes this because it keeps customers trapped in his ecosystem. Backing: future shop inventory. Bank note: closed-loop shop credit.

bowser_bux.name: Bowser Bux
bowser_bux.description: Koopa military scrip backed by fortresses, supply depots, and Bowser’s ability to make refusal feel unwise. Koopa banks accept it cleanly; outside banks apply discounts for political risk and fire damage. Backing: military stores and royal authority. Bank note: bankable in Koopa territory.

shell_credit.name: Shell Credit
shell_credit.description: A Koopa quartermaster credit redeemable for rations, repairs, ammunition, shell polish, and fortress supplies. Banks near Koopa territory accept it because supply credits can be converted into real goods quickly. Backing: warehouse inventory. Bank note: military supply credit.

banana_medallion.name: Banana Medallion
banana_medallion.description: A durable Kong Island token representing stored banana value. It exists because actual bananas vanish before long negotiations end. Banks like it more than fruit and less than gold, which is fair. Backing: stored harvest reserves. Bank note: bankable island token.

coconut_bar.name: Coconut Bar
coconut_bar.description: Pressed coconut oil and fiber value sealed into cargo bars for port exchange. Coastal banks accept it because it stores better than bananas and sells well to ships, kitchens, soap-makers, and potion shops. Backing: stored coconut oil and cargo demand. Bank note: bankable port commodity.

kremling_koin.name: Kremling Koin
kremling_koin.description: A crude raider coin. Most banks refuse it openly, but port banks with private rooms may exchange it at punishing rates after checking whether the coins were recently stolen from their own customers. Backing: stolen metal and raider markets. Bank note: black-market exchange only.

doubloon.name: Syrup Doubloon
doubloon.description: A heavy coin used in pirate ports, shipyards, taverns, and cargo auctions. Legitimate banks discount it; port banks accept it because pretending pirates do not trade has never stopped pirates from trading. Backing: plunder shares and port trust. Bank note: bankable in ports; suspect inland.

cargo_share.name: Cargo Share
cargo_share.description: A draft against a specific cargo haul, prize, or warehouse lot. Banks accept it if the ship, cargo, captain, and dockmaster can all be verified, which means banks accept it less often than pirates claim. Backing: future cargo proceeds. Bank note: conditional port draft.

arcane_shard.name: Arcane Shard
arcane_shard.description: Crystallized magical energy used in enchanting, spellwork, repairs, and academy labs. Guild banks accept shards by grade. Ordinary banks accept them only if a mage signs that they will not explode. Backing: usable magical energy. Bank note: bankable graded component.

guild_seal.name: Guild Seal
guild_seal.description: A stamped Mages’ Guild credit redeemable for components, archive access, repairs, tutoring, containment circles, and sanctioned spell services. It is respectable because the Guild says so loudly. Backing: guild labor and component stock. Bank note: bankable guild credit.

transit_stamp.name: Transit Stamp
transit_stamp.description: A regulated planar transit credit used to reserve portal work, stabilize crossings, or pay emergency return fees. Banks treat it like a high-value travel draft because portal access is expensive and measurable. Backing: regulated portal services. Bank note: restricted bankable travel draft.

kivotos_credit.name: Kivotos Credit
kivotos_credit.description: A stable academy-city credit used for tuition, cafeterias, weapons maintenance, club budgets, and student government emergencies. Midlands banks accept it only through digital-clearing partners. Backing: academy budgets and digital accounts. Bank note: bankable where digital clearing exists.

data_chit.name: Data Chit
data_chit.description: A Millennium Science School chit redeemable for compute time, lab hours, robotics parts, and technical services. Banks exchange it when they can verify the ledger; otherwise it is a shiny rectangle with attitude. Backing: compute access and lab inventory. Bank note: bankable digital service credit.

credstick.name: Credstick
credstick.description: Encrypted portable digital value. Excellent in networked markets, useless in a haunted swamp with no signal. Banks accept credsticks if they can authenticate the ledger and if nobody has chewed the port. Backing: encrypted account balances. Bank note: bankable digital money.

tea_chit.name: Tea Chit
tea_chit.description: A coded Tea Leaf Syndicate chit. Legal banks refuse it at the counter and sometimes clear it through back doors. Big T and Chai understand the marks; that is the difference between currency and suspicious paper. Backing: syndicate ledgers and favor credit. Bank note: private-bank/black-market credit.

broker_mark.name: Broker Mark
broker_mark.description: An underworld mark redeemable for information, introductions, silence, or discreet delivery. It is accepted by shadow banks because secrets are liquid assets if the Broker says they are. Backing: verified secrets and underworld trust. Bank note: black-market bankable marker.

spirit_bead.name: Spirit Bead
spirit_bead.description: A Rakasha bead of shell, bone, amber, or spirit-touched stone. Banks near Rakasha territory accept bead strands by maker and story mark; foreign banks undervalue them because foreign banks lack manners. Backing: craft value and clan recognition. Bank note: bankable cultural token in local markets.

fey_acorn.name: Promise Acorn
fey_acorn.description: A sealed Feywild promise condensed into an acorn. Banks accept it only in branches that understand fey contracts, and yes, Waluigi knows how that sentence sounds. Backing: binding fey obligation. Bank note: restricted bankable fey contract.

court_leaf.name: Court Leaf
court_leaf.description: A gilded Feyward court leaf used for hospitality debts, formal apologies, and witnessed favors. It is bankable only when provenance is intact, because fey money without context is just a leaf with legal teeth. Backing: court favor and etiquette debt. Bank note: restricted court credit.

autumn_leaf.name: Autumnwood Mark
autumn_leaf.description: A provincial mark used in Autumnwood orchards, timber markets, harvest tolls, and local court fees. Banks accept it because Lady Toriel’s administration has made local accounts boring, which is praise in finance. Backing: harvest taxes and timber rights. Bank note: local legal tender.

blood_vial.name: Blood Vial
blood_vial.description: A sealed vial of preserved blood used in vampire markets and certain ritual economies. Normal banks refuse it; Crimson Ledger-style banks accept it by potency, age, source, and whether the clerk survives opening the drawer. Backing: ritual potency and vampire demand. Bank note: restricted occult bank commodity.

soul_coin.name: Soul Coin
soul_coin.description: A lower-plane coin containing a trapped soul. It is bankable only in the worst banks, which means it is very bankable somewhere and should make everyone feel worse about economics. Backing: bound soul value. Bank note: banned except occult banks.

shadow_obol.name: Shadow Obol
shadow_obol.description: Cold Shadow Estate scrip used by servants, hunters, archivists, imps, and other residents of a local economy that considers sunlight an auditing failure. Specialized banks accept it; cheerful banks do not. Backing: local service economy and fear. Bank note: bankable only in Shadowfell markets.

vampire_marker.name: Vampire Marker
vampire_marker.description: A formal favor marker from a vampire house. It is not cash, but old banks understand that enforceable social debt can be priced. The danger is that the price may include you. Backing: enforceable social debt. Bank note: predatory but bankable favor credit.

index_token.name: Index Token
index_token.description: An Archivist token redeemable for indexed records, memory files, auction proofs, and restricted documentation inside Shadow Estate systems. Banks accept it only if they already trade in blackmail. Backing: restricted records and leverage. Bank note: specialized archive credit.

dwarf_oathgold.name: Oathgold
dwarf_oathgold.description: Dwarven gold stamped with enforceable oath marks. Banks love the metal and fear the cultural consequences of mishandling it, which is exactly why Dwarven clients prefer it. Backing: gold weight and oath law. Bank note: premium bank reserve.

warpstone.name: Warpstone Token
warpstone.description: A refined token of magical chaos. Almost every lawful bank refuses it at the counter; arcane black banks buy it through containment windows and charge enough fees to imply moral panic. Backing: dangerous magical power. Bank note: illegal hazardous commodity.

astral_pearl.name: Astral Pearl
astral_pearl.description: A pearl formed in astral currents around divine, psychic, or planar turbulence. Mages, navigators, and high-end banks value it because rarity plus utility equals collateral. Backing: rare planar navigation value. Bank note: bankable rare commodity.

rupee.name: Rupee
rupee.description: A cut gemstone currency from Hyrulean-style markets. Banks accept rupees as gem currency after grading color and clarity, then pretend they understood the color-value chart all along. Backing: cut gemstone value. Bank note: bankable foreign gem tender.

poke_dollar.name: PokéDollar
poke_dollar.description: League-regulated trainer currency used for clinics, travel, prize payouts, and shops. Banks accept it where League accounts can clear; elsewhere it becomes a novelty until a trainer pays in bulk. Backing: league taxes and clinic economy. Bank note: bankable foreign fiat.

mora.name: Mora
mora.description: Teyvat’s common mint coin. It is popular with banks because it has deep trade habits, reliable minting, and enough merchant tradition to make arguments short. Backing: continental trade confidence. Bank note: bankable foreign fiat.

toad_whistle.name: Courier Whistle
toad_whistle.description: A Toad Network token redeemable for courier priority, route notes, civic messages, and small delivery favors. Local banks accept batches from known couriers because movement has measurable value. Backing: delivery labor and trusted routes. Bank note: bankable civic service token.

banking._README: Edit this file to update bank accounts, loans, and debts WITHOUT rebuilding. Just save and refresh the browser.

_INSTRUCTIONS.bank_accounts: Each account needs: id (unique), owner (player name), bankId (from bank list below), currencyKey (from currencies), balance, interestRate (annual, e.g. 0.05 = 5%), depositDate {year, monthIndex, day}
_INSTRUCTIONS.loans: Each loan needs: id (unique), borrower (player name), bankId, currencyKey, principal, interestRate, originDate, termDays, paid (amount repaid so far), status (active/overdue/paid)
_INSTRUCTIONS.debts: Each debt needs: id (unique), creditor, debtor, currencyKey, originalAmount, interestRate, daysBorrowed, amountOwed (current total), status (active/overdue/paid/defaulted), note
